name: Indeterminate Cell Histiocytosis

criteria.description: Presence of histiocytic infiltrate with cells expressing CD1a and S100 but lacking Birbeck granules
Immunohistochemical positivity for CD1a and S100 protein with absence of Langerin (CD207)
Cutaneous lesions characterized by papules or nodules without systemic involvement
Absence of Birbeck granules on electron microscopy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological and immunophenotypic confirmation with clinical presentation consistent with cutaneous lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of Langerhans cell histiocytosis and other histiocytic disorders

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple erythematous to brown papules or nodules
pathognomonic.notes: Typically asymptomatic and distributed on trunk and extremities
searchTerms: multiple red to brown skin bumps

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histologic presence of CD1a+ S100+ histiocytes without Birbeck granules
searchTerms: skin biopsy showing specific immune cells
presence of CD1a and S100 positive cells

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to CNS infiltration
searchTerms: nerve symptoms due to central nervous system

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
Absence of clonal proliferation in peripheral blood
imaging: Usually normal; imaging may be used to exclude systemic involvement
Ultrasound or CT may show lymphadenopathy if present
genetic: Negative for BRAF V600E mutation commonly seen in Langerhans cell histiocytosis
other: Electron microscopy showing absence of Birbeck granules
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD1a and S100, negative for Langerin (CD207)

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of Birbeck granules on electron microscopy
Typically affects infants and young children

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with ulceration
Development of systemic symptoms such as unexplained fever or weight loss
Neurological deficits suggestive of CNS involvement
references: Fraitag S, et al. Indeterminate cell histiocytosis: a clinicopathologic study of 10 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2001.
Weitzman S, et al. Histiocytic disorders of children and adults: introduction and overview. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2015.
